{{convert|29|°C|°F|abbr=on}}{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/324275|title=Soaring temperatures for All-Ireland hurling final day|website=[[HoganStand.com]]|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} | attendance = | previous = [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2021]] | next = [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023]] }} The '''2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 17 July 2022 between [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|135th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. This was the earliest in the year that the final had ever taken place. Some past finals had taken place at dates earlier in the year, but these were finals rescheduled from the years in which they were originally supposed to occur.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/news/gaa-publish-master-fixtures-schedule-for-2022/|title=GAA publish Master Fixtures Schedule for 2022|website=www.gaa.ie}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/1122/1262358-only-championship-finals-will-have-replays-next-year/|title=25-week inter-county season to conclude by late July|first=Damian|last=Lawlor|date=November 22, 2021|via=www.rte.ie}} Reigning title holder Limerick won the game by 1–31 to 2–26 to claim their fourth title in five years and their first ever three-in-a-row.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310723-resilient-limerick-see-off-cats-to-claim-three-in-a-row/|title=Resilient Limerick see off Kilkenny to claim three-in-a-row|publisher=[[RTÉ News and Current Affairs]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kilkenny-all-ireland-hurling-5819034-Jul2022/|title=Limerick complete All-Ireland three-in-a-row after epic contest against Kilkenny|date=17 July 2022|work=The 42|accessdate=19 July 2022}} The game was the joint highest scoring final in history, equalling the total of 66 points scored in the 2021 final between Limerick and Cork,{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242223-all-ireland-shc-finalcork-v-limerick-updates/|title=Recap: Limerick 3-32 Cork 1-22|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=21 July 2022}} and had the most scores (60) in a final, surpassing the 58 scores of the 2021 final. Kilkenny's score of 2–26 was the highest total for a losing team in a final. There were 25 different scorers in the game, 10 for Limerick and 15 for Kilkenny. The match was televised live on [[RTÉ One]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the Croke Park studio with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Liam Sheedy]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]].{{cite web|url=https://presspack.rte.ie/2022/07/16/sport-on-rte-one-rte2-week-29-4/|title=SPORT ON RTÉ ONE & RTÉ2 Week 29|website=[[RTÉ.ie]]|publisher=RTÉ Press Centre|date=15 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} The match was also live on [[Sky Sports]], with analysis from [[Jamesie O'Connor]], [[Ollie Canning]] and [[J. J. Delaney]]. [[Audience share]] for television coverage of the game in Ireland was 72%.{{cite news|url=https://www.kilkennypeople.ie/news/gaa/863368/revealed-how-many-viewers-tuned-into-the-all-ireland-hurling-final.html|title=REVEALED: How many viewers tuned into the All-Ireland hurling final?|work=[[Kilkenny People]]|date=18 July 2022}} ==Background== {{main|Kilkenny–Limerick hurling rivalry}} *This was the first meeting of Kilkenny and Limerick in the final since [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2007]]. They had met in nine previous finals, Kilkenny winning five ([[1911 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1911]], [[1933 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1933]], [[1935 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1935]], [[1974 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1974]], [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2007]]) and Limerick four ([[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1897]], [[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1936]], [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1940]], [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1973]]). *Kilkenny had not won an All-Ireland since [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2015]]; this final marked their seventh season in 2022}} ===Pageantry=== [[President of Ireland|President]] [[Michael D. Higgins]] greeted the players along with the [[GAA President]] for the first time since the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019 All-Ireland final]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland|COVID-19 pandemic]] and the pre-match parade featuring the [[Artane Band]] made a return for a second year running. The [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] was brought out onto the pitch by two Ukrainian children who had fled their country due to the ongoing [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. ===Build-up=== The final was shown on a giant screen at the [[Gaelic Grounds]] in Limerick where an all ticket crowd watched the match.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40918889.html|title=All-Ireland final: TUS Gaelic Grounds to run fan zone for supporters|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican|date=16 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} ===Jubilee teams=== The [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] team that won the [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1996 All-Ireland Final]] along with the [[Clare GAA|Clare]] teams that won the [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1995]] and [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1997]] All-Ireland Final's were presented to the crowd before the match. The first time teams were presented on the pitch since the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019 All-Ireland Final]].{{cite web|url= https://hoganstand.com/Wexford/article/index/324280|title=1990's Clare and Wexford All-Ireland winning teams honoured on All-Ireland final day|date=17 July 2022|work=[[HoganStand.com]]|accessdate=19 July 2022}} ==Match== ===Summary=== In dry and very warm conditions of {{convert|29|°C|°F|abbr=on}} due to a [[July 2022 European heat wave|heat wave]], [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] opened the scoring in the first minute. In front of a crowd of over 80,000 for the first time since the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019 All-Ireland final]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland|COVID-19 pandemic]], [[Gearóid Hegarty]] got the opening goal of the game after four minutes with a strike to the left corner of the net from out on the right to make it 1-1 to no score.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kilkenny-all-ireland-hurling-final-live-score-updates-5819458-Jul2022/ |title=AS IT HAPPENED: LIMERICK V KILKENNY, ALL-IRELAND HURLING FINAL|date=17 July 2022|work=The 42|accessdate=19 July 2022}} Limerick were ahead by four points at half-time on a 1-17 to 0-16 scoreline. In the second half, goals from [[Billy Ryan (hurler)|Billy Ryan]] with a low shot to the corner of the net and [[Martin Keoghan]] with a shot into the left corner form the right twice helped to briefly drag Kilkenny back on level terms, and every one of their subs scored – [[Richie Hogan]] hitting an equaliser in his first appearance of the season. In the end, Limerick won the game 1-31 to 2-26 to claim their fourth title in five years and their first ever three-in-a-row. He lifts it with the injured Cian Lynch. }} In doing so, Hannon became the first captain to lift the Liam MacCarthy Cup four times.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/324283|title=Limerick complete All-Ireland three-in-a-row after sensational final win against Cats|website=[[HoganStand.com]]|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Lynch later revealed that he was not anticipating Hannon asking him to lift the trophy with him.{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/cian-lynch-ankle-injury-2-5820402-Jul2022/|title='You're dealing with grief really, you have to accept it' — Cian Lynch facing three months out with injury|publisher=[[The42.ie]]|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien|date=19 July 2022|accessdate=19 July 2022}} ===Reaction=== Limerick captain [[Declan Hannon]] speaking to RTÉ after the match said "It means everything to us".{{cite tweet|author=RTÉ GAA|user=RTEgaa|title='It means everything to us'. Limerick captain Declan Hannon savours another All-Ireland title following today's victory at Croke Park #RTEGAA. Highlights on @TheSundayGame @RTE2/@RTEplayer from 9.30pm|number=1548722215482531840|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Limerick manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] spoke to RTÉ after the match about how much it meant to make history with Limerick and how the panel almost governed itself in setting standards.{{cite tweet|author=The Sunday Game|user=TheSundayGame|number=1548710370658893831|title=John Kiely talks about how much it means to make history with Limerick and how the panel almost governs itself in setting standards. #sundaygame|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} [[Kyle Hayes]] dedicated Limerick's third All-Ireland SHC title in a row to [[Cian Lynch]], "the heart and soul of our team". Speaking to RTÉ Sport, Hayes said: "Anyone who knows Ciano personally, he's an absolute gentleman."{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310725-hayes-dedicates-glory-to-limericks-heart-soul/|title=Hayes dedicates glory to Limerick's 'heart and soul'|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Kilkenny manager [[Brian Cody]] speaking to RTÉ after the match said "It was close for sure at the end. I think every Kilkenny person should be very, very proud of how the Kilkenny team performed."{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310735-cody-every-kilkenny-person-should-be-proud/|title=Brian Cody: Every Kilkenny person should be proud of how the team performed|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} Highlights of the final were shown on ''The Sunday Game'' programme which aired at 9:30pm that night on [[RTÉ2]] and was presented by [[Des Cahill]] with match analysis from [[Jackie Tyrrell]], [[Brendan Cummins (GAA player)|Brendan Cummins]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]], [[Davy Fitzgerald]], [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]] and [[Ursula Jacob]]. On the man of the match award shortlist were [[Gearóid Hegarty]], [[Kyle Hayes]] and [[Diarmaid Byrnes]] with Gearóid Hegarty winning the award which was presented by GAA president Larry McCarthy at the post match Limerick function at the [[Burlington Hotel (Dublin)|Clayton Burlington Hotel]] in Dublin. ===Celebrations=== The Limerick team returned home the day after the final where the homecoming event was held at [[Gaelic Grounds]], with the team arriving around 7pm. Shortly after 5pm, an estimated 40,000 people turned out to see the team and fans lined a route on an open-top bus from Colbert Rail Station where the team arrived through Mallow Street, O'Connell
